mileage_note: Delhi petrol assumed at about ₹102 per litre. Hill-town prices are often a little higher. Terrain mileage is an estimate for a petrol Mahindra XUV700: highway/plain 12–14 km/l, hill crawl about 9 km/l, uphill about 8–9 km/l, downhill about 13–15 km/l. Mid case is shown; a low–high range is also stored.
osrm_note: Road km come from the public OSRM driving router (router.project-osrm.org). Times from OSRM are optimistic. Realistic hours add a hill buffer and 30 minutes for food and fuel. Photo stops are extra and are listed in each plan.

budget_defaults.meal_note: Assumption for 3 cheap meals a day, about ₹350 per person per day. Change it if your group eats more or less.
budget_defaults.bed_note: A typical cheap hill homestay or dorm bed is often around ₹500–800 in the quieter season. ₹700 is only a planning figure, not a quote.

tips.title: Do not get stuck
tips.body: A 2WD XUV700 is fine on a ploughed, open road. It is not a snow-plough. If the road is unploughed, or police say 4×4 and chains only, turn around. Carry chains, a torch, water and a full tank.

tips.title: Check the road the night before
tips.body: Look at the latest update from the local police, district administration or BRO for that stretch (Manali, Kinnaur, Joshimath, Uttarkashi, Rohru). A Friday plan can be wrong by Saturday morning.

tips.title: Times on this site are honest-but-slow
tips.body: The raw router times are optimistic. The ‘realistic’ hours already add a hill buffer and 30 minutes for food and fuel. Photo stops are extra, and are written into each day plan.

tips.title: Fuel, not just scenery
tips.body: Fill up in the last proper town — often Manali, Reckong Peo / Bhabanagar, Joshimath, Uttarkashi, Rohru or Vikasnagar. Do not count on a pump in a high village.

forecast_note: Snow figures come live from the Open-Meteo weather model, using each place’s real elevation. They are model estimates, not a person standing in the village. A short flurry can be missed; a forecast can be wrong. The time on the grid is when this page last fetched the data.

plan.title: Shaheen Bagh to Manali
plan.body: Long plains-then-hills day (about 10–11 hours with food and photo buffers). Leave at dawn. Eat at a NH44 dhaba, then Mandi or Aut. Night in Manali so you are not crossing to Lahaul in the dark.

plan.body: Manali to Sissu is much shorter. Go through the tunnel in daylight. Walk the lake and waterfall, take photos, and turn around if police limit 2WD traffic. Night in Sissu if rooms are open, otherwise back to Manali.

plan.title: Home, or one extra snow morning
plan.body: If the sky is clear, a short morning walk, then the long drive home. Do not start the Delhi stretch after mid-afternoon.

side_trips.note: Estimate about 30–45 min in real hill traffic if the pass is open.

spots.snow_months: The pass (about 3,140 m) often holds snow from December to March and is often closed then. Jibhi village is much lower (about 1,780 m) and gets less snow.

spots.name: Chanshal / Dodra Kwar

side_trips.note: About 1.5–2 hours extra, only if the pass is officially open.

spots.snow_months: The pass (about 3,760 m) can hold snow from November into spring, and is often closed for a long mid-winter stretch. Dodra Kwar, beyond the pass, can be cut off.
spots.safety: This is the highest road on the list. A 2WD SUV should not attempt Chanshal Pass with fresh or packed snow. Go only when Rohru locals and the local administration say the pass is open and ploughed or dry. There is almost no recovery once you are on the top. Dodra Kwar is a further 36 km after the pass.

spots.corridor: This map’s driving route is Delhi → Dehradun → Chamba (Uttarakhand) → Karnaprayag → Auli / Joshimath. Many drivers instead go via Rishikesh and Devprayag. Compare both the night before.

spots.name: Harsil
spots.safety: Beyond Uttarkashi on the Gangotri road, along the Bhagirathi river. The road can close after heavy snow or landslides. A 2WD SUV is usually fine when the road is open and ploughed. Fill fuel in Uttarkashi. There may be checkpoints. This page is about the valley and riverside villages, not a temple run.
spots.stay_where: Harsil, or nearby Bagori / Dharali if you find a bed.

plan.title: Shaheen Bagh to Uttarkashi or Harsil
plan.body: Realistic one-way about 9–10 hours. You can reach Harsil the same day if you leave at dawn and the road is open. Otherwise night in Uttarkashi and go up in the morning.

plan.title: Valley villages and the river
plan.body: Walk Harsil, Bagori and the riverside in daylight. This is a slow valley, not a checklist.

plan.body: Full day back. Start early.

spots.name: Chakrata
spots.snow_months: Typically December to February, and not every year — it is the lowest ‘snow’ town on the main list, so treat snow as a bonus, not a promise.
spots.safety: Closest high village from Shaheen Bagh. Forest roads can be narrow and foggy. A 2WD SUV is usually fine in clear weather. After a rare snow, roads ice over. The Tiger Falls spur is a side road — go in daylight. Fill fuel in Dehradun or Vikasnagar.

plan.body: Realistic one-way about 6 hours, so a late-morning start still works. See Tiger Falls in daylight. Night in Chakrata.

plan.title: Deoban or Chilmiri, then home
plan.body: A ridge walk or viewpoint in the morning, then drive back to Shaheen Bagh the same afternoon.

spots.name: Hatkoti
spots.snow_months: The village itself is about 1,420 m, so it is not a snow destination. Higher roads towards Rohru and Chanshal may have snow in mid-winter.
spots.safety: A Pabbar river village on the Jubbal–Rohru belt. The hill road is fine for a 2WD SUV in dry weather. After heavy rain, watch for slips. This is a riverside stop, not a high-pass drive.

spots.name: Tiuni
spots.snow_months: The town is about 935 m, so snow in the bazaar is uncommon. Higher side-roads can see winter snow.
spots.safety: On the Tons, on the Paonta–Rohru road (NH707). Hill road with some rough stretches, fine for a 2WD SUV in dry weather. Fill fuel before the long hill section (Dehradun / Paonta / Vikasnagar). Services in town are modest.

spots.name: Mori
spots.snow_months: The village is about 1,180 m, so it is a river destination, not a snow bowl. Higher forests around Govind Pashu Vihar get winter snow.
spots.safety: An offbeat Tons village past Tiuni, in the Govind Pashu Vihar area. The valley road is narrow. A 2WD SUV is usually fine in dry weather. Services are limited — fill fuel at the last proper pump you pass (often before or at the Tiuni / Purola side; check on the day). Do not drive this road at night in rain.

spots.name: Shivpuri & Kaudiyala
spots.snow_months: River-level (about 370–440 m). No snow here. Come for the Ganges, not for a white landscape.
spots.safety: The Rishikesh–Badrinath river road is usually open and is fine for a 2WD SUV. Weekends are busy with rafting traffic. Park only in safe, obvious spots. This is not a snow drive.
